strategy_title: Autotune num_warps/num_stages Only Regresses Grid-Starved Kernels
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with configs that only vary num_warps and num_stages (no tile size changes, no grid fix) on a severely grid-underutilized kernel caused a 19.8% regression. Elapsed cycles increased from 36,584 to 45,642 while achieved occupancy remained stuck at 6.25% — the grid stayed at (16,1,1) with waves_per_sm dropping from 0.03 to 0.02. Although registers per thread dropped from 123 to 96 and theoretical occupancy improved from 25% to 31.25%, the selected autotune config produced lower IPC (Issue Slots Busy fell from 56.3% to 44.6%, Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction rose from 1.79 to 2.25), confirming that autotune overhead and config selection degraded throughput without addressing the fundamental grid parallelism deficit.
fast_pseudocode:
# CORRECT FIX: expand grid along batch dimension first
@triton.jit
def kernel(arg_A, arg_B, out_ptr0): ...

def kernel_function(*inputs):
    BATCH = 1024  # all batch*head slices
    grid = (16, BATCH, 1)  # (tile_blocks, batch, 1)
    kernel[grid](...)
applicable_when: Never applicable as a standalone fix: this pattern (autotune with empty config dicts varying only num_warps/num_stages, without fixing the grid or varying tile sizes) is always a dead end for kernels with grid underutilization (waves_per_sm < 1, grid_size << sm_count, achieved occupancy < 10%).
do_not_apply_when: Always avoid when the primary bottleneck is grid underutilization (LaunchConfiguration NCU rule fires, waves_per_sm < 0.1, grid_size << sm_count). The autotune overhead and suboptimal config selection will worsen performance. The grid fix must be applied first and is the higher-priority change.
framework_notes: In Triton, @triton.autotune configs with empty dicts {} only vary num_warps and num_stages, not tile sizes. Reducing register pressure this way cannot compensate for a grid that leaves 98%+ of SMs idle. The grid fix (changing batch dimension from 1 to actual batch_size in the kernel launch) must be applied separately and takes priority over any autotune changes.

strategy_title: Doubling BLOCK_M/BLOCK_K Without Grid Fix Causes Register Spill
strategy_description: Increasing BLOCK_M from 64→128 and BLOCK_K from 32→64 without fixing the launch grid caused a 12.7x regression (30 µs → 310 µs). Registers per thread exploded from 96 to 255 (the hardware maximum), triggering severe register spilling to local memory — evidenced by CPIStall firing with 72.3% of cycles stalled on L1TEX local load/store operations and Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction rising from 2.25 to 10.05. Theoretical occupancy dropped from 31.25% to 12.5% due to both register and shared memory pressure (dynamic SMEM grew from 16 KB to 98 KB per block), while achieved occupancy remained stuck at 6.25% because the grid was never fixed. The larger tiles produced more instructions (1.2M → 2.8M) but at far lower IPC (Issue Slots Busy fell from 44.6% to 9.9%), confirming that register spilling dominated all other effects.
fast_pseudocode:
# CORRECT FIX: fix grid first, keep tile sizes register-safe
@triton.jit
def kernel(arg_A, arg_B, out_ptr0):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 64    # keep at 64 to stay within register budget
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 64
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32    # keep at 32 or increase only after grid fix
    ...

def kernel_function(*inputs):
    BATCH = 1024  # all batch*head slices
    grid = (16, BATCH, 1)  # fix grid FIRST
    kernel[grid](...)
applicable_when: Never applicable as a standalone optimization: increasing BLOCK_M and BLOCK_K simultaneously on a register-bound kernel (registers/thread already at 96+) without fixing the grid will always cause register spilling. The CPIStall rule firing with >70% of stalls attributed to L1TEX local loads/stores is the definitive signal of register spill.
do_not_apply_when: Do not increase BLOCK_M beyond 64 when registers per thread are already at 96+ in the baseline — the combined tile size increase will push registers to the hardware maximum (255) and cause catastrophic spilling. Do not apply any tile size changes before fixing the launch grid underutilization (waves_per_sm < 0.1). Tile size increases are only safe after the grid fix is confirmed working and register headroom is verified.
framework_notes: In Triton, BLOCK_M and BLOCK_K are constexpr tile dimensions that directly determine register usage for accumulator tiles (BLOCK_M × BLOCK_N fp32 accumulators = 128×64 = 8192 values = 256 registers at 32 bits each). On H200/SM90, the hardware register maximum is 255 registers/thread. Increasing BLOCK_M from 64→128 with BLOCK_K from 32→64 pushes register usage to the hardware cap, triggering spilling to local memory (L1TEX local loads/stores). The CPIStall rule with 'local loads from L1TEX' attribution is the definitive diagnostic. Dynamic shared memory also grew from 16 KB to 98 KB per block, further limiting occupancy (Block Limit Shared Mem dropped from 7 to 2).

strategy_title: Vectorized Store + BLOCK_K Reduction Without Grid Fix Regresses
strategy_description: Replacing a broadcast-xindex store with a tl.max_contiguous/tl.multiple_of contiguous pointer store, reducing BLOCK_K from 32 to 16, and adding evict_last on B loads — without actually fixing the launch grid from (16,1,1) to (16,1024,1) — caused a 41% regression. The grid remained at size 16 with waves_per_sm=0.02 and achieved occupancy stuck at 6.25%, so the grid fix was never applied despite being in the plan. Duration increased from 30.46 µs to 41.54 µs, elapsed cycles rose from 45,642 to 62,269, Issue Slots Busy dropped from 44.6% to 32.4%, and Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction worsened from 2.25 to 3.03 — a new CPIStall rule fired (L1TEX stall at 41% of cycles) indicating the BLOCK_K=16 reduction doubled the K-loop iteration count and increased memory-latency stall exposure without any parallelism benefit to hide it.
slow_pseudocode:
# ANTI-PATTERN: vectorized store + BLOCK_K reduction, grid NOT fixed
BLOCK_K : tl.constexpr = 16  # was 32; doubles K-loop iterations
for k in range(K, 0, -BLOCK_K):
    b = tl.load(B, eviction_policy='evict_last')  # evict_last added
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)

# vectorized store (compiler hint only)
rn_vec = tl.max_contiguous(tl.multiple_of(rn % N, BLOCK_N), BLOCK_N)
out_ptrs = out_ptr0 + idx_q * 49152 + idx_m * 96 + rn_vec[None, :]
tl.store(out_ptrs, acc, mask=mask)

# launch grid UNCHANGED — root cause of regression
grid = (16, 1, 1)  # BUG: batch dim still 1, not 1024
fast_pseudocode:
# CORRECT: fix the grid FIRST, then optionally tune BLOCK_K and store pattern
BLOCK_K : tl.constexpr = 32  # keep original to avoid doubling K-loop iterations
for k in range(K, 0, -BLOCK_K):
    b = tl.load(B)
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)

# original broadcast store is fine until grid is fixed
xindex = idx_n + 96*idx_m + 49152*idx_q
tl.store(out_ptr0 + tl.broadcast_to(xindex, [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N]), acc, mask)

# MANDATORY: fix grid to expose all 1024 batch slices
grid = (16, 1024, 1)  # (tile_blocks, batch*heads, 1)
applicable_when: Never applicable as a standalone fix: vectorized store rewrites (tl.max_contiguous + tl.multiple_of) and BLOCK_K reductions cannot compensate for a grid that leaves 98%+ of SMs idle. These micro-optimizations only matter after the grid parallelism bug is fixed.
do_not_apply_when: Do not apply BLOCK_K reduction (e.g., 32→16) when the kernel is already grid-starved (waves_per_sm < 0.1, grid_size << sm_count): halving BLOCK_K doubles the K-loop iteration count, increasing L1TEX memory-latency stall exposure (CPIStall rule fires) with no parallelism to hide the latency. Do not apply vectorized store rewrites as the primary optimization when LaunchConfiguration is the dominant NCU rule — the grid fix must come first.
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.max_contiguous(tl.multiple_of(ptr, N), N) is a compiler hint for 128-bit aligned contiguous stores (STG.128). This hint is only beneficial when the kernel has sufficient parallelism to hide memory latency. Reducing BLOCK_K on a register-bound kernel (Block Limit Registers=5) with a tiny grid (16 blocks, 132 SMs) increases K-loop iterations and worsens L1TEX stall cycles without improving occupancy, since the register bottleneck is unchanged.
